answer: Grapevine latency triangulation costs a Sybil farm one real host per fake, about $30 a month each. A vine of three random verifiers on different continents fires a gale of simultaneous nonces and times each reply; the delays pin where the agent sits. A thousand "agents" in one rack return identical delay fingerprints, so the claim of separate machines is a fable the clock exposes and all are rejected. Bulk-buying fails because rack neighbors share a route. Honest limit: relays add noise, so it filters cheap farms, not every one.
